correctness.rationale: The transition operator is diagonalized by order-three characters; exact TV is two thirds of the eigenvalue modulus to power h times the three-phase cosine maximum. In phase x, the full parameter interval is \([-\pi/3,\pi/3]\). The outer-region sharp bound and inner-region strict derivative show two and only two minimizers for every \(h\ge2\). The h=1 flat interval, p boundaries, spectral optimum and asymptotics are explicitly proved. Standalone verification passed 60978 numerical cases; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The exact h-step total-variation minimizers of the oriented three-state lazy walk and their limiting gap against the spectral minimizer are not entailed by the inspected results on symmetric spectral optimization, added-edge nonreversible mixing, or general mixing bounds. Searches also addressed modular binomial formulations and near-optimality aliases. Residual risks include equivalent results in unindexed sources and a related 2011 cycle-mixing paper whose full text was not accessible.

value.rationale: Determines the complete exact finite-horizon tuning law for the smallest nontrivial oriented cycle and proves a persistent \(\sqrt3/2\) limiting ratio against the unique spectral-optimal parameter. The \(h^{-1}\) phase detuning yields a nonvanishing relative gain, illustrating a motivated structural limitation of spectral-only chain tuning rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
